title: MeshCore Open · Images over LoRa
description: Share AI-reconstructed images over a low-bandwidth MeshCore network. MeshCore Open encodes a small representation on the sender and reconstructs a similar image on the receiver. Reconstructed details may differ from the original.
author: MeshCore Open community / Seeed Studio
setup: Install a MeshCore Open app release that supports image transmission, following the current project documentation.
Connect a compatible MeshCore node, configure the LoRa region and network, and prepare a second node as the receiver.
Enable image transmission and download the machine-learning model files in app settings.
Choose an image and send it. The receiving app reconstructs the image from the compressed representation.
Use reconstructed images for general scene awareness; they are not exact copies suitable for evidence or precise image analysis.

title: EasySkyMesh · Low-Power Mesh Firmware
description: Build low-power sensor networks with EasySkyMesh, a community firmware based on MeshCore. Add power-saving features and supported I2C sensors to Wio Tracker L1 for remote monitoring and off-grid experiments.
author: IoTThinks / EasySkyMesh community
setup: Connect Wio Tracker L1 to a computer with a USB data cable.
Download an EasySkyMesh release matching your board and installation type.
Open the MeshCore Web Flasher, choose Custom Firmware, select the file, and enter DFU mode when prompted. Flash and reboot.
Configure the regional radio settings. Companion power saving is enabled by default; repeaters and room servers require the powersaving on CLI command.
Connect supported sensors with the correct voltage and I2C wiring; follow the project sensor guide.
